svg.title: Diffusion / Flow Matching vs Direct Quantile Output
svg.desc: Generating sample paths to trace a distribution versus computing quantiles in one shot — and what that means for path-dependent risk.
svg.text: Diffusion · flow matching vs quantile output
Build a distribution from samples, or compute the quantiles directly
Cross-time dependence lives in the samples
They cannot be stitched into paths
The distribution exists only once the paths are collected
The quantile bands come out immediately
Each step's interval is read off at once
Questions it can answer — whole paths
Exceeds c at least once in the period
Scenarios and risk figures come from the same output
Questions it can answer — per time step
Exceeds c at least once in the period
Generative models build paths into a distribution; a quantile head computes each interval directly.
The quantile head wins on speed; the generative route on expressiveness and paths.
No collection of per-step quantiles recovers the distribution of the period's maximum or minimum.
Next (S12): GIFT-Eval vs real backtests — the traps of leakage, frequency and finance.
